transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Yeah… I guess I came in because my head just hasn’t been working right lately. Like at work, I’ll be sitting with a client and suddenly realize I’ve lost the thread of what they were saying, even though I’m trying to listen. And then I’ll look at a chart note and read the same line over and over, like when you reread a menu even though you’re not hungry—sorry, that’s not really related.

It’s just… simple decisions I used to make without thinking, I kind of freeze on now. It’s been making work feel really hard.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

I’m… not really sure. I don’t know what exactly counts as “depressed,” you know? Like, I wouldn’t say I have a clean answer where I can point to it and go, yes, that’s what it is.

I’ve been kind of not myself, I guess. But then I start overthinking the word “down,” because some days I can still talk to people and get through things, and then I wonder if I’m making too much of it. Sorry, that probably doesn’t answer it very directly.
Have you been enjoying things less than usual lately?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t really do the stuff I normally do. My guitar’s just been sitting in the corner, and every time I look at it I think I should pick it up, but then I just… don’t.

I’ve been bailing on soccer too, and the shelter shifts, which I used to feel good about. And even when I try to do something, like cook something decent or go hiking, it feels kind of pointless, like I’m just doing the steps because I remember I’m supposed to like it.
For much of the day lately, have you been feeling sad or low?

I don’t know… “sad” feels like a really specific word, and I’m not sure I’d put it that way. Low, maybe? But then I think of low like when your phone battery is at 12% and you’re trying to decide if you should plug it in now or wait, which is probably not what you mean.

I guess for a lot of the day I feel kind of… flattened out. Not exactly crying or anything. Just not up. Sorry, I’m not sure if that answers it.
Did something stressful happen in your life around the time these problems started?

Yeah, I think so. It kind of started about a month ago, around when the clinic lost some staff and everything got reshuffled.

My schedule moved into late-evening coverage, and there’s been a lot more crisis paperwork. Which sounds boring when I say it like that, but it really changed the whole rhythm of my days. Like, I used to know when I’d be home, and now I’m doing notes late and thinking about forms and coverage and… sorry, I’m getting off track. But yeah, that was around when this started.
Have you been feeling anxious or on edge a lot lately?

I’m not sure. Like, “on edge” maybe sometimes, but I don’t know if I’d call it a lot. I’ve always had this thing where if a notification pops up, I kind of immediately look at it, which probably says more about phones than anxiety, right?

Lately I guess I’ve been… keyed up at moments, but it’s hard to separate from just being tired or distracted. I don’t think I’ve really been walking around panicky or anything. Sorry, I know that’s not a clean answer.
Have you noticed your sleep has changed lately?

Yeah… sleep’s been weird. I’ll get home really tired, like I should just be able to pass out, but then I’m lying there for hours kind of replaying the whole day in my head.

It’s stupid stuff sometimes, like remembering one note I wrote or something someone said, and then somehow it turns into thinking about tomorrow, and then I look at the clock and it’s way later than I thought. And even when I do fall asleep, I’ve been waking up before my alarm feeling like I barely slept.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot more than usual?

I don’t know if it’s “a lot more.” I mean… I worry, sure, but I feel like everyone worries when work gets messy. Like, even my roommate was saying the other day that he checks his email before bed, and I was like, see, that’s just normal now.

But for me, I’m not sure it’s exactly worry so much as my brain just keeps picking things up and putting them down again. Like I’ll think about one thing, then something totally unrelated, and then I’m like, why am I thinking about grocery bags right now? Sorry. I guess I haven’t really noticed it as some big increase, no.
Have you been moving or speaking more slowly than usual lately?

I don’t think so? I mean, I haven’t really noticed myself talking slower. Sometimes I’ll pause because I’m trying to think of the right word, but I feel like I’ve always done that, like in school presentations and stuff.

Moving slower… maybe if I’m tired, but not in a way where someone’s said anything to me. I don’t know. I guess I haven’t been paying attention to that specifically.
Have you been feeling hopeless lately?

I’m not sure. I mean, “hopeless” sounds really big, you know? Like a movie version of it or something.

I guess I have moments where I’m like… what am I even doing, but then I’ll get distracted by something stupid, like realizing I never folded my laundry, or I’ll start thinking about this guy from high school who always seemed to have everything planned out. I don’t know why that popped into my head.

So… I don’t know if I’d call it hopeless exactly. Maybe I just haven’t really thought about that word.
Have you had any thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of hurting yourself?

I don’t… I don’t have like a plan or anything. I’m not sitting there figuring out how to hurt myself.

But yeah, I’ve had thoughts like… if I just didn’t wake up, maybe that would be easier. And then I get freaked out because I know that’s not just some random thought, you know? Like, I’ll be brushing my teeth or staring at my phone, and it’ll just kind of show up, and then I’m thinking about how people say stuff like that and it means something bad, and then I feel weird for even thinking it.

So… yeah. Not a plan, but the thoughts are there, and they scare me.
Have these symptoms been present most days for at least two weeks?

Yeah… I think so. It’s been most days, for probably about a month now.

It kind of started when the clinic lost some staff and my schedule got shifted into more late-evening coverage. And then the crisis paperwork got heavier too, which… I know sounds like just a work thing, but it’s sort of when I noticed everything started feeling like this. Like before that I was busy, but this has felt different. So, yeah, definitely more than two weeks.
Have you noticed your appetite has changed lately?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t really feel hungry most days unless someone points it out, like “did you eat?” and then I’m like, oh, I guess I didn’t.

It’s weird because I used to be kind of routine about meals, or at least snacks. I had this whole thing where I’d buy the same sandwich from the place near work, and the guy there knew my order, which sounds depressing in a different way, but now I’ll just… forget. Or not forget exactly, I just don’t feel like eating.

And my pants have been looser, so I guess I’ve been skipping meals more than I realized.
Lately, have you been feeling worthless or overly guilty?

Yeah… yeah, I think that’s been happening a lot.

Like if I miss one little detail in a note, or I don’t return a call right away, my brain just goes straight to, “You’re useless, you’re letting everyone down.” And it’s not even always a huge mistake. Sometimes it’s just something small, like I forgot to add one thing and then I’m thinking about how the whole clinic probably has to clean up after me, which… I know that sounds dramatic.

It’s kind of like when you get one of those group emails about “please remember to do the thing,” and even if it wasn’t about you, you feel like it was absolutely about you. I do that constantly now. With clients, coworkers, everybody. I keep feeling like I’m failing them somehow.
Do these feelings seem stronger than you’d expect just from the work changes?

Yeah… I think they are stronger than just, like, “work is stressful.”

I mean, everyone misses things sometimes, right? Like a note detail or not calling someone back immediately. At the clinic there’s always some form that has six different boxes and one of them is apparently the important one—sorry, that’s not really the point. The point is, when I do it, I don’t just think, “Okay, fix it.” I go straight to, “I’m useless. I’m letting the clients down. I’m letting everyone at the clinic down.”

It feels bigger than the actual thing I did. Like my reaction doesn’t match the mistake.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day nearly every day lately?

I… I don’t know how to measure “most of the day,” honestly. Like, I wouldn’t say I’m crying all day or anything like that. It’s more like… I wake up and there’s this heaviness, and then I go do what I’m supposed to do, and sometimes I get distracted by something random, like a client’s scheduling form or whether I left my mug in the staff room again.

So… yeah, maybe? I’m not sure. I feel low a lot, but I don’t know if it’s every day in the exact way you mean.
Over the past month, have you felt down or depressed nearly every day?

I’m not totally sure. Like, I’ve definitely felt down a lot this past month, but “nearly every day” makes me feel like I should be able to count it, and I haven’t really been keeping track.

Some days I get through things and I’m just kind of… flat, I guess. Other days I don’t notice it as much until later, like when I’m sitting there after work and realize I’ve been in that low mood for hours. But I don’t want to say yes if I’m not sure what you mean by nearly every day.
In the past month, have you felt low or down on more days than not?

I think… probably? But I’m still kind of hesitating because “more days than not” sounds simple, and then my brain starts trying to make it exact.

Like, I remember a bunch of days feeling low, especially when I’m just going through the day and everything feels heavier than it should. But I didn’t mark it on a calendar or anything. I used to do that for workouts for like two weeks, actually, and then I forgot, so I’m not great at tracking stuff.

So… I guess my best answer is that it feels like it’s been happening a lot, maybe more days than not, but I’m not completely sure.
During the past month, have you felt low or down nearly every day?

I’m still not sure I can say “nearly every day” with confidence. It’s been a lot, yeah, like it kind of follows me around, but then I get caught up in things and I don’t always notice it the same way.

I know that sounds vague. I guess I’m stuck on the wording. Like, if I had a calendar, maybe I could tell you, but I don’t. My week kind of blends together sometimes—work stuff, laundry, forgetting to buy toothpaste, that sort of thing. So… I’ve felt low many days, but I don’t know if I can honestly say nearly every day.
If the staffing and schedule changes at work had not happened, do you think you would still be feeling this way?

I mean… probably not in the same way, no. It really feels like it started around when the clinic lost staff and my schedule got shifted into late-evening coverage, plus all the extra crisis paperwork.

It’s been, like, about a month now. Which is weird because at first I kept thinking, “Okay, this is just a rough week,” and then suddenly it was every week. I was even joking with someone that my laundry schedule is more predictable than my actual work schedule now, which is… not that funny, I guess.

So yeah, I think the work changes are a big part of why I’ve been feeling this way.

target_item.reason: The question asks specifically about depressed mood nearly every day, but the provided symptom profile does not include a depressed mood item; the closest listed items cover other symptoms like guilt, sleep, fatigue, concentration, and duration.

patient.answer:
I’m not totally sure. Like, I’ve definitely felt down a lot this past month, but “nearly every day” makes me feel like I should be able to count it, and I haven’t really been keeping track.

Some days I get through things and I’m just kind of… flat, I guess. Other days I don’t notice it as much until later, like when I’m sitting there after work and realize I’ve been in that low mood for hours. But I don’t want to say yes if I’m not sure what you mean by nearly every day.

doctor.intent: Clarify whether the patient has a persistent depressed mood nearly every day, to distinguish major depressive episode from adjustment disorder or nonspecific anxiety/attention problems.
doctor.question: In the past month, have you felt low or down on more days than not?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about depressed or low mood over the past month, but the provided symptom profile does not include a specific item for depressed mood.

patient.answer:
I think… probably? But I’m still kind of hesitating because “more days than not” sounds simple, and then my brain starts trying to make it exact.

Like, I remember a bunch of days feeling low, especially when I’m just going through the day and everything feels heavier than it should. But I didn’t mark it on a calendar or anything. I used to do that for workouts for like two weeks, actually, and then I forgot, so I’m not great at tracking stuff.

So… I guess my best answer is that it feels like it’s been happening a lot, maybe more days than not, but I’m not completely sure.

doctor.question: During the past month, have you felt low or down nearly every day?

patient.answer:
I’m still not sure I can say “nearly every day” with confidence. It’s been a lot, yeah, like it kind of follows me around, but then I get caught up in things and I don’t always notice it the same way.

I know that sounds vague. I guess I’m stuck on the wording. Like, if I had a calendar, maybe I could tell you, but I don’t. My week kind of blends together sometimes—work stuff, laundry, forgetting to buy toothpaste, that sort of thing. So… I’ve felt low many days, but I don’t know if I can honestly say nearly every day.

doctor.question: If the staffing and schedule changes at work had not happened, do you think you would still be feeling this way?

target_item.name: Duration
target_item.manifestation: This has been going on for about a month, since the clinic lost staff and my schedule shifted into late-evening coverage and heavier crisis paperwork.
target_item.reason: The question is asking whether the symptoms are tied to the timing and circumstances of the staffing and schedule changes, which is covered by the duration item noting they have been going on for about a month since those work changes.

patient.answer:
I mean… probably not in the same way, no. It really feels like it started around when the clinic lost staff and my schedule got shifted into late-evening coverage, plus all the extra crisis paperwork.

It’s been, like, about a month now. Which is weird because at first I kept thinking, “Okay, this is just a rough week,” and then suddenly it was every week. I was even joking with someone that my laundry schedule is more predictable than my actual work schedule now, which is… not that funny, I guess.

So yeah, I think the work changes are a big part of why I’ve been feeling this way.
